newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. Council extends Haiti force for four months.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Council extends Haiti force for four months.

text.p: The United Nations Security Council on Wednesday unanimously voted to renew the U.N. military and police operation in Haiti for a final four months but reduce its numbers.

The 15-member council would cut the international police force to 250 from 300 and reduce the military to 50 headquarters staff from 500, paid for by all U.N. members. But Canada and Pakistan will again supplement the U.N. operation with another 1,000 soldiers, financed by Ottawa and Washington.

Canada will contribute 650 troops and Pakistan 350 in arrangements designed to meet Chinese and Russian objections to a more costly force. Beijing, which this time raised no objections, had twice threatened to veto the operation unless its unless its numbers were reduced, prompting Canada to rescue the mission by paying for its own soldiers and securing U.S. financing for the Pakistani troops.

Since the previous renewal was billed as the final extension, the Council changed the name of the mission for the third time. The latest name is the U.N. Transition Mission in Haiti or UNTMIH with a mandate expiring on November 30.

One of the operation's main tasks was to train and monitor Haiti's fledgling police, which replaced the previous paramilitary contingents loyal to the military junta that overthrew elected President Jean-Bertrand Aristide in 1991.

Aristide was restored to power three years later by a U.S.-led 22,000-member multinational force. The United Nations took over peacekeeping in March 1995 with 6,000 troops, a number that has been steadily reduced since then.
